The dragon did not move.

Neither did I.

That seemed fair for the first few seconds.

Then it became his choice.

I had just told a creature older than my kingdom that the future he remembered me not being part of had happened with me in it once already.

There were several reasonable responses to that.

Disbelief.

Questions.

Eating me.

I had prepared for two of those.

Ithar stared.

I shifted my weight off the bad leg.

The movement was small.

His eye followed it anyway.

Eventually he said, “Not this time.”

“Yes.”

“You chose those words.”

“I did.”

“Why?”

“Because they were short.”

His nostril opened.

Not quite a sigh.

I had started assigning meanings to the nostrils.

That was probably dangerous.

“Say what you mean without protecting it with brevity.”

I looked at him.

“That sounds expensive.”

“I have not charged you.”

“Yet.”

“Greg.”

That was the first time my name sounded different in his mouth.

Not important.

Not friendly.

Placed.

Not important.

Not friendly.

Placed.

Like he had put it somewhere and intended to find it again.

I rubbed my thumb across the edge of my rank pin.

The Authority mark caught against the nail.

Low B-class.

Named Ranker.

Peg-Leg Greg, according to people who had never asked whether I wanted the fucking thing attached to me.

Ithar watched the hand.

Of course he did.

“I remember another life,” I said.

Nothing happened.

I had expected that sentence to feel larger.

It did not.

It sounded exactly like what it was.

A man in a cave saying something impossible.

Ithar waited.

I had learned enough to know that meant he was not finished.

“How much?”

“Of the life?”

“Yes.”

“Most of it.”

“Most is a word humans use when they wish to avoid discovering what is missing.”

“I remember forty years.”

“Exactly?”

“No.”

“How nearly?”

“Close enough that I resent the question.”

“That is not a measure.”

“Approximately forty years.”

One corner of his mouth shifted.

I pointed at him.

“Don't.”

“I said nothing.”

“Don't.”

“I said nothing.”

“You were going to.”

“No.”

That was worse somehow.

“Beginning when?”

“Nineteen.”

“Ending?”

“Fifty-nine.”

His eye moved over my face.

Then lower.

The ruined leg.

The right hand that no longer closed all the way.

The shoulder that sat slightly wrong under my coat.

“You are fifty-nine now.”

“Yes.”

“So you remember approximately forty years beginning at the age you first became an adult and ending at your present age.”

“That's one way to make it sound suspicious.”
